chunks: ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who stood in salat (prayer) and forgot to say the takbīr, so he began with the recitation. He said: If he remembers it while standing, before he performs rukuʿ, then let him say the takbīr; and if he has already performed rukuʿ, then let him proceed in his salat (prayer).

The proper way regarding these reports is that we interpret them as applying to one who doubts the opening takbīrah and does not remember it with certainty. So if this is his state, then he says the takbīr so long as he has not yet performed rukuʿ, as a precaution; but once he has performed rukuʿ, he proceeds in his salat (prayer), because he has moved to another state. But if he knew with certain knowledge, then repeating the salat (prayer) would be required of him, according to what we have already presented in the earlier reports.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer under discussion
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةِ الِافْتِتَاحِ: the opening takbīrah that begins the salat (prayer)
key_terms.رَكَعَ: he performed rukuʿ, entering the bowing position
key_terms.يَشُكُّ: to be in doubt and lack certainty
key_terms.يُكَبِّرَ: to pronounce the takbīr, specifically saying 'Allāhu Akbar'

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone forgets Takbīrat al-Iftitāḥ in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of one who begins salat (prayer) and omits the opening takbīrah. The apparent permission to continue if one remembers after rukuʿ is understood as applying to doubt rather than certain omission, while certain omission requires repeating the salat (prayer).
